mostWorthwhile.text: Sending the distant rubble world past the cluster star was most worthwhile: it showed how an intact body can lose its planetary system without being captured by another star.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first encounter was a fairly predictable setup for the more consequential passing-star encounter, though it established why the rubble world was vulnerable.

surprise.text: The rubble world escaped both stars, while a separate portion of the distant ice became bound to the passing star; the outcome depended on their motions and positions, not their composition.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary: the giant first changed the rubble world's orbit, and both subsequent encounters involved the passing star in the distant region.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested in seeing what happens to the sunless world and the ice around its new star, because their different outcomes left distinct paths to follow.
